audit.head: 1d3f6bcc96613c8a3a920141018a45dbb970729c
audit.evidence:
requirement_violation: At HEAD 541b724e9beef66f868d83a87f7049ddc126fb41, src/packages/datacenter/facilityScene/dataCenterFacilitySceneConnections.ts:1984-2025 groups trunks by network and plant ID and emits one common-prefix trunk per group. Its radius is clamp(0.06 × sqrt(connection count), 0.115, 0.35), not a function of thermal duty. The reference implementation repeats this at dataCenterMaksimReferenceScene.ts:1078-1106. Thus header-row count does not determine the number of mains, and changing served duty without changing logical connection count cannot change their width. doc/product-requirements.md:216-223 instead requires one pair per duty-unit row per independent train and radius proportional to sqrt(served duty). The matching sizeDataCenterCoolingTrunksV1 function exists at dataCenterFacilityEquipmentSizing.ts:283-299, but the repository search found callers only in coolingTrunkSizing.test.ts:2-11; neither scene implementation uses it.
collateral_defect: src/__tests__/coolingTrunkOracle.ts:25 drops each entire connection that has carrierRouteIds. However, src/product/facility/facilityScene.ts:8644-8657 removes only its shared carrier prefix and still renders its downstream branch. Consequently the consolidated geometry oracle omits those rendered branches from route counts, lengths and crossing checks. Additionally, coolingTrunkOracle.ts:46,60 measures outside-shell distance only for a rectangular boundary named reference-building; adaptive polygon shells are not measured, so their outsideShellMetres remains zero regardless of exterior route geometry. coolingTrunks.test.ts:11-23 then asserts these incomplete measurements and never enforces the documented trunk-derived polyline bound. This leaves the adaptive-layout and complete-route acceptance obligations in doc/product-requirements.md:225-230 unenforced by this oracle.
